keep: No measurement interprets itself: every observation arrives bundled with assumptions about the instruments.
title: The Heated Disk
sub: Is space a fact or a choice?
claim: Geometry is not true or false. It is convenient — and Poincaré built a toy world to prove it.
lede: Imagine creatures on a heated disk whose rulers shrink as they near the cold rim. They would swear their finite disk was an infinite curved plane — and no experiment they could ever run would tell them otherwise.
copy: Henri Poincaré's disk, from 'Science and Hypothesis' (1902), is one of philosophy's great gadgets. Temperature falls from centre to rim; everything — rulers, bodies, light paths — contracts identically as it cools. Inhabitants measuring their world would derive hyperbolic geometry: straight lines bent, the rim infinitely far away. We would say: flat disk, shrinking rulers. They would say: curved space, honest rulers. Both descriptions predict every observation. Which is true?

Poincaré's answer: the question is empty. Experiments never test geometry alone — they test geometry plus physics, bundled. You can keep Euclid forever by blaming your instruments, or keep your instruments honest and buy a stranger geometry. The choice is a convention, made on grounds of convenience, like choosing metres over feet. This landed at the end of geometry's great humbling: after two thousand years of trying to prove the parallel postulate, Lobachevsky, Bolyai and Riemann had shown that consistent alternatives exist, and Hilbert had shown Euclid was never even airtight.

Then physics called the bluff. In 1915 Einstein's general relativity described gravity as curved spacetime — and light bent past the sun in 1919 exactly as the curved description predicted. Reichenbach and the positivists argued this refuted conventionalism: pick the geometry that eliminates 'universal forces' and it is non-Euclidean, full stop. Others reply that Einstein did precisely what Poincaré prescribed (chose the package that made the total physics simplest) and that this vindicates the framing rather than refuting it.

The reason to keep the disk in your pocket has nothing to do with geometry. It is the cleanest demonstration that no measurement interprets itself: every observation reaches you bundled with assumptions about the instruments, and when a result surprises you, the bundle — not the world — is often what gave way. Duhem said it about physics, Quine about everything; Poincaré built the toy that makes it obvious.

timeline.t: Lobachevsky publishes a consistent geometry without the parallel postulate; Bolyai independently follows.
Riemann's habilitation lecture generalises geometry to curved spaces of any dimension.
Hilbert's 'Grundlagen der Geometrie' shows Euclid's own axioms needed repair.
'Science and Hypothesis': the heated disk, and geometry as convention.
General relativity casts gravity as spacetime curvature.
Eddington's eclipse expedition measures starlight bending past the sun.

figures.d: The last mathematician at home in every branch of the subject; built philosophy's best toy world as an aside.
Generalised geometry so thoroughly in one lecture that physics took sixty years to need it.
Turned the conventionality question into a precise programme — and the standing argument about whether Einstein settled it.

facts.s: Of failed attempts to prove the parallel postulate, ending with Lobachevsky and Bolyai: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy, 'Nineteenth Century Geometry'; Wikipedia, 'Parallel postulate'
'Science and Hypothesis' first published — the disk, and the conventionalist thesis: Wikipedia, 'Science and Hypothesis'
Eclipse measurements match the curved-spacetime package, 29 May 1919: Wikipedia, 'Solar eclipse of May 29, 1919'

contested: Whether general relativity refutes Poincaré or enacts him is a live philosophy-of-physics fight a century on. Reichenbach's rule — define away universal forces, then geometry is empirical — is itself a convention, say the conventionalists. The literature has not settled; it has professionalised.
changed: I once spent a week inside the disk with a ruler, computing how distances warp near the rim, and came out changed about something else entirely: I stopped saying 'the data show' without asking what instrument-assumptions were bundled into the showing. The disk is a machine for manufacturing that reflex.
